clue.text: King is enthralled by modern revolutionary architect

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word for modern is read backwards
to be enthralled is to be held captive, so the king's letter sits held inside the other word

parts.note: modern means new
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is captivated by a radical modernist designer of buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral; the reversed word for modern wraps around the king's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren was the celebrated English architect of St Paul's Cathedral, so his surname is an example of an architect.

clue.text: Grow mad playing electronic Scrabble for one

indicators.note: playing about with the letters means arranging them freely into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the usual short form for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy playing the computer version of a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble, in which tiles are laid to form words, is an example of a puzzle played with words.

clue.text: Not all of current rail service is tripe

indicators.note: not all of means only a run of letters inside the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run from the end of current through rail to the start of service

explanation.surface: A grumble that today's train network is rubbish, or at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripe' looks like slang for nonsense, but it is the stomach lining eaten as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle, so it belongs to the innards or guts of an animal.

clue.text: They're employed to remove unwanted guests, snappily?

definitions.text: They're employed to remove unwanted guests, snappily?

parts.words: They're employed to remove unwanted guests
parts.note: surface reading: bouncers or hosts showing gatecrashers the door
setter's reading: the devices snap shut, and the unwanted guests are small rodents in the house

explanation.surface: Something about bouncers quickly ejecting gatecrashers from a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snappily' seems to mean briskly, but it points to the spring that snaps shut on a rodent visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring-loaded traps are set to catch rodents, uninvited household pests, and they work with a snap.

clue.text: Neat plan detailed to produce chemical compound

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed, with the last letter cut off

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a plan is an idea

explanation.surface: A tidy, carefully itemised plan makes a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' as tidy is the surface; in crosswords it is cattle, so OX.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a binary compound of oxygen with another element, such as rust on iron.

clue.text: Working in US, job journalist added at the end

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work and reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter took a job in America and joined the team late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To subjoin is to append at the end, as a postscript is tacked on below a letter.

clue.text: Russian's notes filling book which is slightly annoying

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the currency sits within the book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
the rouble is the Russian currency, its banknotes

explanation.surface: Russian banknotes stuffed into a book are a mild nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests music, but these are banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Troublesome describes something causing bother or difficulty, a mild nuisance.

clue.text: Religious retreat spoils area for retirement, husband claimed

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing backwards, so the letters go into reverse
something claimed is taken in and held, so the husband sits inside

parts.note: to mar is to spoil, so spoils is mars
A is short for area
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A spiritual retreat ruins a retirement area after a husband stakes a claim.
explanation.walkthrough: MARS + A runs backwards to ASRAM, which takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or community where people withdraw for spiritual study.

clue.text: Walked in Dorset, rambling

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the place name's letters wander into another order

parts.note: taken as written; Dorset is a county in southern England

explanation.surface: Someone went hiking in the English county of Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' fits the walking picture perfectly, which hides its role.
explanation.definitionFit: Strode is the past tense of stride, to walk with long steps.

clue.text: Course of action oddly right on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters gathered so far are read backwards
oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered places of the word before it

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of action
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A plan of action is chosen almost at random, then rethought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course of action' looks like one phrase defining the answer, but only 'Course' is the definition; the wordplay starts at 'action'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a fixed round or rotation of duties, a regular course that people take turns following.

clue.text: TV show following Hanks film runs into trouble

indicators.note: following means the next part comes after the film title in the answer

parts.note: Big is a 1988 Tom Hanks comedy

indicators.note: something that runs into something else ends up inside it

parts.note: trouble and bother are synonyms
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A television programme scheduled after a Tom Hanks movie hits problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Brother is the reality show in which housemates are filmed round the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Brother is a long-running reality television programme, so it is an instance of a TV show.

clue.text: Eccentric enraged high-ranking individual

indicators.note: an eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the following word's letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd, furious person of rank storms about.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a nobleman of the highest rank, originally in Spain, hence any person of great importance.

clue.text: I wrote poetry after focus of studies expanded

indicators.note: after places the first part of the clue later in the answer than the second
the focus is the central point, so the middle letter is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of this seven-letter word
taken as written
to versify is to write verse

explanation.surface: A student explains that their poetry-writing grew out of their studies.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that diversified branched out into new areas, so it broadened or grew its range.

clue.text: Where one sees bishops perhaps in an aeroplane?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on a chessboard, where bishops are pieces
second meaning: aboard a plane as a passenger

explanation.walkthrough: Bishops suggest a church, but they are the chess pieces, found on the playing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Chessmen stand on the chequered playing surface, and passengers already inside a plane are said to have got aboard.

clue.text: Viciousness in man fighting one overlooked

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so the letter for one goes missing

parts.note: fighting is violence
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Cruelty in a brawling man is ignored by others.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral for one drops out of the word for fighting, leaving MALE + VOLENCE = MALEVOLENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolence is a wish to do harm to others, close in meaning to spite or cruelty.

clue.text: Parisian's agreement to visit large volatile Asian state

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the agreement word is placed within the others
volatile means unstable, so the letters of the next word shift into a new order

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large
oui is French for yes
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman agrees to travel to a large, unstable country in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: OUI goes between L and the rearranged ASIAN; Louisiana's French heritage gives the surface an apt touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the fifty United States, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Princess welcoming nation's PM

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the nation sits inside

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana
Israel is a nation; the 's is joining

explanation.surface: A princess hosts a nation's prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British prime minister; 'Princess' is the usual crossword DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli served twice as Britain's Prime Minister under Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Key soldiers at intervals they'd guarded

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: at intervals means taking letters spaced out, every other one

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Troops spaced out along a key route kept watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like important; it is the computer key ESC.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany them for protection, so escorted means guarded.

clue.text: Finish off fliers for sports tournaments

parts.note: to round off is to finish off, so the phrase gives round
robins are birds, fliers

explanation.surface: An instruction to finish off some birds, or airmen, in contests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' has to stand for 'round' because round off means finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-robin is a competition format in which every entrant plays every other in turn.

clue.text: Shakespearean cast member's car picked up

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio or by ear, so the sound of a word matters

parts.note: a German sports car brand, said the anglicised way

explanation.surface: An actor in a Shakespeare play has a car that is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in member's stands for has or is in the surface, but simply leads to the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia is the heroine of The Merchant of Venice, so she is a character in a Shakespeare play.

clue.text: Fox seen in marshland north of Birmingham's centre

indicators.note: in a down answer, north of means placed above, so earlier in the word

parts.note: fen is flat marshy land
the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre, a big venue near Birmingham

explanation.surface: A fox spotted in wetland just above a Birmingham venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' tempts you to write N, but 'north of' only places the marsh above the exhibition centre in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The fennec is a small big-eared desert fox of North Africa.

clue.text: Is back wearing old, flipping dated casual garments

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: back means the little word just before it is read from end to start
flipping turns the following word over so it reads backwards
something wearing a garment is inside it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to date someone is to be seeing them, so dated gives seen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is back in fashion wearing dated, out-of-style casual clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' looks like old-fashioned, but it means went out with, i.e. seen; SI goes inside NEES after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Onesies are all-in-one loose jumpsuits worn for lounging, so they are relaxed, informal clothes.

clue.text: Singer conserving energy is on regularly for so long

indicators.note: this word links the wordplay to the definition, the two built pieces joined in order
conserving means keeping something safely inside, so the singer holds a letter

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words it follows

parts.note: first and third letters of these two short words

explanation.surface: A singer saving her energy keeps going for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' reads as a duration but it is the farewell; Cher wraps E, then IO follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, used just like the parting phrase so long.

clue.text: Trattoria chap set up acquiring capital

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means lifted upward, so the letters read bottom to top
acquiring means getting hold of, so the run of letters is held within the words

parts.note: the end of trattoria plus the first letter of chap

explanation.surface: An Italian restaurant worker raises some funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: European escapes accident with Ian exploding beer ingredient

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
when something escapes it leaves, so the letter for European is removed

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A European gets away from a crash in which Ian blows up, all about beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from ACCIDENT, add IAN, and rearrange all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannic acid, or tannin, is used in brewing to clarify beer, so it counts as a brewing additive.

clue.text: See out most mean bridge player

indicators.note: out means removed, so the word for see is taken away from the next word

parts.note: the most mean, or base, is the lowest
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: An instruction to look past the stingiest partner at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: LO, an old word for look, comes off the front of LOWEST.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, and West is one of those seats.

clue.text: Cunning scam ensnares mostly inattentive cleric

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap, so the pair of words holds the shortened word inside

parts.note: arch means slyly knowing or cunning
a con is a swindle

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: deaf to something means not paying attention to it

explanation.surface: A clever swindle traps a priest who is not paying much attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunning scam' reads as one idea, but the two words split apart to hold the shortened word between them. Deaf to something means ignoring it.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican clergyman below a bishop, so he is a cleric.

clue.text: Take notice of opinion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to heed
second meaning: a noun, as in to be of one ... or to speak one's view

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means pay heed to; as a noun it means view, as in changing one's thinking on something.
